title: Fill and drain with timers in Ladder
summary: Run one fill, hold and drain cycle of a tank with TON blocks in rungs, a panel start and an emergency stop.
scope: The grade runs the simulated tank in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real tank, valve or sensor, its timing or its safety.
objectives: Time one step of a process with an on-delay timer (TON), using one timer for each step.
Use a timer as a safety limit on a step that normally ends on a sensor, and let an emergency stop abort the cycle.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: The scene is a tank with a fill valve, a drain valve and a low-level switch, a Start button, an emergency stop and a stack light. In src/TimedTank.ld.json, run one cycle for each press of Start while the emergency stop is released and the tank is idle: amber on, Fill open for a time set by a timer (the tank has no sensor at this level, so the timer is the measurement), a two-second hold, then Drain open until LevelLow or twenty seconds, then green on. The emergency stop closes both valves and lights red.
stages.checkpoint: The cycle is a chain of steps and each timed step has its own timer.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, predict the outputs at {{t:100}} ms (before the press), at {{t:800}} ms (the cycle has started) and at {{t:1500}} ms (the emergency stop is pressed). Then predict where the cycle stands at {{t:25000}} ms, after a second press at {{t:4000}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: {{v:TimedTank.Fill=false,TimedTank.Drain=false,TimedTank.Green=false,TimedTank.Red=false@100|Everything OFF}} at {{t:100}} ms; {{v:TimedTank.Fill=true,TimedTank.Amber=true,TimedTank.Green=false@800|Fill and Amber ON}} at {{t:800}} ms; {{v:TimedTank.Fill=false,TimedTank.Drain=false,TimedTank.Red=true@1500|both valves closed and Red ON}} at {{t:1500}} ms; {{v:TimedTank.Green=true,TimedTank.Drain=false,TimedTank.Red=false@25000|Green ON and the drain closed}} at {{t:25000}} ms.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: The starter has no rungs: no valve ever opens, so the cycle never runs. It declares the inputs and outputs. Keep a step number (0 idle, 1 fill, 2 hold, 3 drain) in an INT variable, one TON block for each timed step, and drive the outputs from the step with one rung for each output. The fill lasts 3.5 seconds: a TON block with PT of T#3500ms.
stages.checkpoint: The program has a step variable, three timers and one rung for each output.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press Check. ZPLC runs src/TimedTank.ld.json against the tank of scene timed-tank, presses Start, operates the emergency stop and presses Start again, and tests {{assertions}} assertions: the outputs at fixed times, and that the tank never spills.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named timed-tank and contains {{assertions}} assertions and passes them all.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Watch the tank fill while Amber is on, hold, then empty until the low switch. Relate the emergency stop at {{t:1000}} ms to the step: the cycle goes back to idle, so the press at {{t:4000}} ms starts a new one.
stages.checkpoint: The trace shows a first cycle aborted at the stop and a second cycle that ends in Green.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: A timer measures time, not volume: if the fill valve were slower the tank would hold less after the same 3.5 seconds. The drain waits for a sensor and the timer only limits the wait.
stages.checkpoint: Name the step where a timer replaces a sensor and the step where it backs one up.

hints.text: Each timer rung starts with a comparison of the step: an EQ box on Step and 1 feeds a TON block with PT of T#3500ms, and when its Q is TRUE a MOVE box writes the next step.

One rung for each transition: an EStopOk contact in normally closed form feeds a MOVE of 0 to Step, and EStopOk, an EQ of Step and 0, and Start feed a MOVE of 1. Then HoldT for two seconds and DrainT for twenty seconds, whose exit rung needs LevelLow OR the DrainT output. Finally one rung for each output: Fill when Step is 1, Drain when Step is 3, Amber when Step differs from 0, Red when EStopOk is off, and Green is TRUE after a finished cycle.

faultCases: The starter has no rungs: no valve ever opens, so the cycle never runs.
